title: What the Covered Grain Keeps

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The first reading sets the figure. The second sets it where the first stood and calls the setting new. The sack under wool has no voice in either; the hand that filled it keeps what no slate can take.
epigraph.attribution: A rack-end saying, told over covered grain before the second reading of Smoke

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and fifty-eight to two hundred and sixty days, six months and seventy-eight days to six months and eighty days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing — the file turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the body inventoried as a wound of crust, gap, frozen thread, cold and afterdrop in the order they arrive; the district's second reading heard as a chart turned face-down over covered grain, the printed figure kept beside the paid and the heard bell beside the told, neither laid across the other; the hand's six answerings kept as honest objects and never promoted into a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a payment, a held change, a key, a power or a rule — with no present-tense Chicago break and no tagged remembered line; the old life stays offstage, and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room or back-room interior, no seventh hearing, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no sixth asking and no witness for the row question, no tenth record-first hand, no eighth green or eighth shape, no third gap, no name spoken over either sighting, no sale, no calling of the loan, no naming of a payer, no private record opened, read or copied, no figure given for the covered grain or for the hand that did not come back, no lesson made of the one opening before Smoke 1, no third Account-day brought early, and no ending.

scenes.title: The Nineteenth Morning
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, first dated \daymark (Smoke 19, Ninthday) and the chapter's only drop cap on the opening words: small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey at the hearth, the kiln mouth, the drying racks, the rack end and the yard well. Open with the hand laid down against the fold on the ninetieth answer; set it down like a tool put away, never recalled as a sign, growth, reaching, gift or power. Count carried at 257 exact, six months and seventy-seven days, told by nobody, coming into 258, six months and seventy-eight days (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and fifty-eight days, its payer unnamed (T088). First smell hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the unswept corner called the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. Three counts in three places — the kiln's four low pulls and silence under the floor, the river's water over water through the finger's-width door, the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — none rising into another, for agreeing any two would want a payer and none stands (T061/T082). Body inventory in the old order: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread frozen and unwiped; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform; he knows the severe face cold wears and wants the crust, both true and the second louder, entered nowhere (T060/T086). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, tells it the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along a two-gapped row without a figure, and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed (T100, T058/T079). The dressed grain lies covered under wool on the cool stone at the rack end away from the hearth; she lifts a corner for damp and lays it back, and it gains no figure, so that the arithmetic to be read over it on Smoke 20 will not know what it cost (T077 advanced, unpaid). Frost on the well lip has gone grey under the bucket and the yard calls it weather; he keeps the white lip on a place of its own with no cause — not a payer, not the widow's mark (a well is not an opening) and not the first firing of Frost (T083/T085 carried). A neighbour's cost-question goes to the pot and the weather; a number in a fist comes up toward the well and goes back into a sleeve, arriving nowhere (T015/T041/T047 held). Smoke 20 stands one morning ahead and is not brought into a day that has not earned it. Hand answer ninety-one: down at once on the river's next low note, an object on the sixth place and not a reach, hearing, seventh, payment, held change, key, power or rule (T061/T082). Last image: the covered grain under wool at the rack end with the corner laid back and no figure on it; the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand; the hand resting against the fold.

scenes.title: The Places Gone Around
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 258, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the Clay Yard's walked-around places, the yard well and bare trough, the drying racks and the space under the lowest rack, the pan's gone round ring, the worked strips and the terrace, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the back room heard only as a direction, the clay road at the going of the light, the bed and the towel. Afternoon thins without ending; heat settles into the fold; one crust two inches off with its gap unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint; afterdrop waiting (T061/T082). Garl is kept in objects, a keeping and not a story, his name unspoken two hundred and fifty-eight days — salt-stiff coat on its peg with the left-shoulder crease, hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack, the tile debt circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with; no collector comes up or goes down the clay road (T009/T013/T092). Sella carries the basket at the half-pace from every open slate and goes wide around seven things, each with a look and a wide step and no number: the clean dark line and the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone ring, the bare dark trough with its water called weather, the field's empty place out on the worked strips, and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, gone around with a look and no name (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried, not paid). Ilva is glimpsed at the well drawing with the pail against her knee, clay pale in her nail crescents and rack dust in one thumb seam; her hand stays in her sleeve, the notched birch strip is not taken out, read, asked about or joined to the reed-cutter's cord, and she answers the question put with her mouth — Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account — so no tenth hand is filed and the ninth stays nine (T080 held). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after its instruction, says Yes, house to the early thaw and the late while keeping the late because it puts off the paying, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, sets the knife at the very lip with six where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, keeps Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, and brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name — a remembered ninth stopping, no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath drawn and not spent, the loan uncalled, chest tight, Ash in the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring holding what light there is, the warm stone cold and unreconciled in its unmarked loft pot, and his stroke over the bright patch and the collector road without the half-check or a turn of the head (T036/T076, T006). At the wheel-shed edge Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust past the bent finger and white in a fist's creases, parts dusty forearms from clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate broke nor whether it was a birth-slate; three or more men go low before first grey into the finger's-width-open back room and get no name from him and he does not say the room is cold; he speaks to the wheel before any person — It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady — tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withholds it on the near-full tray (T061/T082); the three pot sayings stay three with the premature note from Smoke 14 on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause, the burned-slate word stays at four from Slate Row and the two shut-room tellings at two, his promise of the boy's name stays ungiven and he's not Vail stays sealed (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095), and when Sella's sentence goes low his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of it and holds until the end arrives at the pot (T062). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen, tells the fire the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it and goes to her own bed; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs, untouched since before the kiln on Smoke 1, and the one opening before Smoke 1 stays behind the household with no lesson, no sign and no payer (T058/T079). In the small hours he turns the file out on the towel and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers, three pot sayings with the premature note apart, four low things with water over water a fifth, told bell beside heard and told figure beside paid with Smoke's first arithmetic locked up the road, nine stoppings with no tenth, three held changes plus the loft scrape, the pale line and the held inch on six places, nine record-first hands with Ilva's ninth on its own tray, the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth, the covered grain unfigured, the pan's ring and the other absences on trays that do not touch, and the ownerless question at five askings with no witness and no row named (T061/T082, T101 held). Hand answer ninety-two: held for the small intake only and down before the letting-go, borrowing no house count, an object and not a power (T061/T082). Last image: the towel laid on the fold with every tray parted and every gap left gap, and the hand laid back against the fold as a tool put away.

scenes.title: The Second Reading
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated \daymark: Day 259, Smoke 20, Tenthday, Y.H. 813, the second Account-day and market of the second firing, from the small hours under the Vail roof up the clay road to the Cross and the reading block under the moot-post, through the square and the pot board, down to the out-of-line landing below the north bridge, and home at the going of the light. New day, new date, no recap: 259 exact, six months and seventy-nine days, nobody told (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and fifty-nine days (T088); the widow's mark untouched since Smoke 1, because a market and a reading are not openings (T058/T079). Smoke 20 comes on its own morning, earned by that light, and was not brought into Day 258. Sella carries him up at the half-pace from every open slate, sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lies, stands half a pace off and gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket; eight pigs go over the wet boards and two hundred lean in. Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, the smell of nothing at all under the hot clay; he wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure, reads one in twelve, as the notice says twice over the basket — once for the moot and once for the households that came late — calls the levy, denies it with your house, never I, sends a number to a slate at the watch and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness. The district's arithmetic changes for the second time in Smoke and cannot be changed back; the printed figure stands unchallenged, the figure read is still not the figure paid, the space between the figure read over the covered grain at home and what that grain cost has no signature, and the reading answers nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 or the hand that went in on Seed 15 (T015/T041/T047, T077, T098 carried). The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself; the heard bell stays beside the told and is not made a seventh of the full note (T078). Hessa Rale takes the slate up the road toward Greybank before noon with hand to slate before eye to crowd and the writing turned to her sleeve, answering the question put and not the one behind it — I don't read it. I carry it. There's a difference, and the road doesn't care which; Cross to Greybank. Reading goes up before noon. I've got a road to walk — no figure coming off it, her reaching the eighth hand on its own tray and no tenth filed (T080). Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, the market selling over him as water over a stone (T090). Across the square at the pot board a silent woman turns a cup a quarter and sets it back, sweet lead-glaze green at one corner of her mouth and a pale line across the back of one hand kept on its own place; at the market's edge a small shape in cast-offs catches the light on a green sliver, grins with a gap and turns its head a half-beat late toward a set-down pot. Both are sightings only: a colour and a shape on places of their own, with no eighth or ninth, no name, no loaf, no slate, no sale, no joining and never Fenna or Ulda in the narration (T050/T051 and T033/T034 held). Hand answer ninety-three: held through the gap where the bell's next stroke did not come and down on the stroke after it, supplying no stroke to fill the gap and making the heard bell no seventh, an object on the sixth place (T061/T082). Sella lifts the basket out of the shade at the going of the light, carries him home at the half-pace and sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, says nothing of what was read over him. Last image: the basket up the clay road with the reading block empty behind it and the bell's gap still unfilled under the roof.

scenes.title: The Figure the Grain Cannot Answer
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 259, no new dated heading: the small hours under the Vail roof, the bed, the loaf shelf and the towel, with the kindling and the wheel-shed reaching the basket only as sounds and directions. Afternoon has thinned and the house is quiet; one crust two inches off with its gap unnamed and no third, the thread frozen and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint, the afterdrop waiting (T061/T082). He turns the file out as a surgeon turns instruments out on a towel and finds the whole of it exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The day's arithmetic is behind and unread under this roof: Berr's narrow slate and locked box are up the clay road, Hessa's slate went up unread, the clerk's inward slate stays at the landing, and none was opened, copied or brought near the basket. The figure read is still not the figure paid; the dressed grain lies covered under wool on the cool stone at the rack end, changed in state and carrying no figure, and the space between the figure read over it and the price of that grain still has no signature to lay on it. He keeps the two figures on two places and does not average them, because a thing covered is not therefore paid for and a thing not entered is not therefore free (T015/T041/T047, T077). The rest of the file is unchanged: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh and none invented to fill the empty place, three near-full answers and three pot sayings with the premature note of Smoke 14 on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause, the burned-slate word at four and the two shut-room tellings at two, told bell beside heard and told figure beside paid, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, three held changes plus the loft scrape and the pale line on five places, the held inch on a sixth, nine record-first hands with Ilva's ninth on its own tray and her stick unread in her sleeve, the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth, the pan's gone ring and the other walked-around absences on trays that do not touch, the ownerless question at five askings with no witness and no row named (T061/T082, T080 held, T101 held, T060/T086, T098 carried). Tarn's ear-sentence came to the word that would call the loan and stopped as a remembered stopping with no figure and no name; the loan stayed uncalled, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the warm stone cold in its pot. Jorra's bent finger waited at the cold damper ahead of an unfinished sentence as a remembered fraction, his promise of the boy's name neither given nor withdrawn and he's not Vail sealed (T036/T076, T006, T035/T031/T062). The second reading answered nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 and no name was given to what ailed him; no collector came for Garl's tile debt or for the hand that went in on Seed 15. Hand answer ninety-four: one rhythm carried across the wall that does not touch, taking the little silence after a count that had ended in the other room as an object in its own right, crossing no second count and filling nothing, and down on the river's next low note — an answer and not a reaching (T061/T082). Last image: the towel laid on the fold with the covered grain's lack of a figure kept on a place of its own and nothing signed on the space between figure and cost.

scenes.title: The Week After the Reading
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated \daymark: Day 260, Smoke 21, Firstday, Y.H. 813, the small hours under the Vail roof, then the ordinary morning at the hearth, the drying racks, the rack end, the loaf shelf, the boards and the yard well. New day, new date, no recap: 260 exact, six months and eighty days, told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and sixty days, its payer unnamed (T088); the widow's mark touched once before the kiln on Smoke 1 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, morning, afternoon or dusk since (T058/T079). First smell hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the thaw; first sound the kiln in fours with its gap, no bell, no market and no Cross. Smoke 30 (Day 269), the third and last Account-day of the second firing, stands nine mornings ahead and is not brought early; the first firing of Frost (Day 271) is far off and unbrought. The third working week begins as an ordinary tending that has learned nothing from the reading: Sella goes to the fire before the basket, tells it the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, lips along the two-gapped row without a figure, and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed (T100). The dressed grain is turned under wool for damp and laid back on the cool stone at the rack end, changed in state and given no figure; yesterday's arithmetic read over it did not know its cost, and he keeps that as a finding with no payer, not a grievance with a debtor (T077 advanced, not paid). Frost has gone out of the well lip under the bucket and the yard calls the whole of it weather; the rope takes the cold and the pail comes up grey, and he keeps whatever white was there on a place of its own with no cause — not an opening, not the widow's mark and not the first firing of Frost (T083/T085 carried). A neighbour's cost-question goes to the pot and the weather and a fist-number comes up toward the well and goes back into a sleeve, so no figure arrives and none is supplied (T015/T041/T047 held). Hand answer ninety-five: kept to the river's own interval with no house count to borrow, down on the next low note, an object on the sixth place (T061/T082). Last image: the covered grain under wool at the rack end with a corner lifted for damp and laid back and no figure on it; the pot handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand; the hand resting against the fold.

scenes.title: The Ninety-Sixth Object
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 260, Smoke 21, Firstday, afternoon into the small hours at the Clay Yard, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the back room as a direction and a sound, the clay road at the going of the light, the bed and the towel. Smoke goes on without a boundary drawn in the narration and neither of the district's two names for the months is set right or left wrong. Afternoon thins without ending; heat into the fold; one leathery brown-edged crust two inches off with its empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint; afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform (T061/T082). Garl is kept in objects, name unspoken two hundred and sixty days, the tile debt neither paid nor settled nor done with, no collector up or down the clay road on Smoke 19, 20 or 21 (T009/T013/T092). The walked-around places are gone around with a look and a wide step and no number, including the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out (T098 carried). Sella carries him up at the going of the light at the half-pace from every open slate, goes wide around the seven places, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen, tells the fire the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening and goes to her own bed; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs and the one opening before Smoke 1 stays behind the household with no lesson, no mending and no payer named, the next real opening being the first firing of Frost far off (T058/T079). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom after its instruction, says Yes, house and Six counted. The next I don't count, sets six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, brings the ear-sentence to the calling word and stops there as a remembered ninth stopping with no figure and no name, no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled, Ash in the knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring holding what light there is, the warm stone cold in its loft pot and the small dry loft-sill scrape on a place of its own (T036/T076, T006). At the wheel-shed edge Jorra comes through with meal-fine dust past the bent finger, gives the men who went into the back room before first grey no name and does not say the room was cold, speaks to the wheel before any person, tells a pot You'll do and withholds its note three turns ahead on the near-full tray; the three pot sayings stay three with the premature note of Smoke 14 on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause, the burned-slate word stays at four and the two shut-room tellings at two, the promise of the boy's name stays ungiven and he's not Vail stays sealed, and his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence (T035/T031/T062, T061/T082, T065/T095). In the small hours he turns the file out on the towel and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh and none invented, three near-full answers, three pot sayings with the premature note apart, burned slate at four and shut-room tellings at two, told bell beside heard and told figure beside paid with Smoke's second arithmetic now behind and unread up the clay road, nine stoppings with no tenth, three held changes plus the loft scrape, the pale line and the held inch on six places with six honest answers standing on it, nine record-first hands with Ilva's ninth on its own tray and her stick unread, the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth, the covered grain unfigured, the absences on trays that do not touch, and the ownerless question at five askings with no witness and no row named (T061/T082, T080 held, T101 held, T015/T041/T047, T077). Hand answer ninety-six: held one rhythm for the small intake and let it go, then carried one rhythm across the little silence after a count that had ended in the room that does not touch as a second object in its own right, neither interval laid across the other, and down on the river's next low note — an answer and not a reaching, filed on the sixth place with no payer named, not a longer reach, miss entered as a finding, hearing, seventh of the full note, tenth stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule (T061/T082). Two hundred and sixty stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Sarn, Sill or Grath; six months and eighty days are told by nobody; ninety-six honest answers stand on the sixth place and none of them is a reach; the carried fire stops at four with its fifth unpaid the same number of days and its payer unnamed; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs; the grain lies covered and unfigured; the seventh year stands at its very end and has not given. The file lies open with every tray parted and every gap left gap. Smoke goes on without a boundary drawn, and the count goes forward into Smoke 22, a day that has not earned its heading; Smoke 30 stands nine mornings beyond the close and is not reached for, and the first firing of Frost stands far off and unbrought. Last image: the hand laid back against the fold on the ninety-sixth answer, an object and not a power, while the count goes forward into Smoke 22.
